what_the_eye_sees: Better than round 1: the whole band is now beaded, with no bald metal. It still does not read as a lizard. At 300 px it reads as a sea-urchin shell or a caviar/granulation band. The beads are separate round pearls on visible land, so they look applied rather than grown. The only pattern is bead size: fields of big pearls against fields of fine pearls, set in rectilinear blocks and columns. From the face, rows of larger beads also fan out diagonally from the stone in an X, which is exactly the ambulacral star of an urchin test with the stone as its boss. Nothing reads as banding that forks and merges. No dorsal bead line runs along the crest, and the fat-tail swell barely registers. A jeweller would say 'granulated band with an orange stone, sea-urchin style' and would not name a Gila monster or any reptile.
changes: Replace the blocky size-contrast pattern with Gila banding carried by height and shadow on one uniform lattice. All flank and shoulder zones (theta 35 to 145 and 215 to 325, crest to edge fillet) use one pitch, and the big-bead and fine-bead blocks go. Redraw the 'Reticulation' mask as irregular transverse bands, 3 to 5 beads wide, that fork, merge and waver, with no straight edges and no rays from the stone. Delete the diagonal X of large beads that radiates from the spessartite. High beads 0.36 mm, low beads 0.24 mm cushion-remapped, as the section specifies. Acceptance: in hero-300 and face-300 you see dark, shadowed, blotchy crossbands that branch like a Gila's markings, with no square block, column or star centred on the stone.

Close the land so the hide looks like pebbled skin rather than loose pearls. Cut the bead land from about 0.42 x pitch to about 0.20 to 0.25 x pitch across the Beadwork group. Flatten the crowns toward the crest (theta 90 +/- 40) into low, slightly polygonal shingles that touch their neighbours, and keep full domes only in the outer third toward the edge fillets. Acceptance: at 300 px, bright metal land shows only as thin seams between beads. Near the crest the beads read as flat-topped tiles, and at the edges as rounder domes.

Make the dorsal bead row and the swell visible. Run one continuous line of about 1.1 mm domes, 0.42 mm high, along crest_v through the spessartite, which is its central bead. The line should be at least 1.5 x the neighbouring beads in size and stand clear of the band pattern on either side, tapering in size away from 90 degrees. Push the keyframed swell at theta 90 so the face visibly fattens compared with theta 35 and 145, for example width 1.22 to about 1.30. Acceptance: in face-300 a single horizontal bead spine runs left to right through the stone, and in hero-300 the top of the band is visibly thicker than the flanks, like a fat tail.
